pairs.subject: eval-harness
pairs.evidence: apps/console/src/pages/simulator/Verdicts.tsx:137 The verdict page names the judge only by a tier alias (`judge · ${v.judge_tier}`; the JudgeVerdict contract carries no resolved dated model id or rubric/packet version) and offers a different tier as the guard against bias, but a sonnet judge scoring a haiku candidate is the same model family, which judge-stability calls a conflict of interest, and an unstamped alias cannot tie a drift to any instrument.

techniques.evidence: apps/console/src/pages/simulator/Verdicts.tsx:133 The judge is shown only as a tier alias (the technique: a tier name is an alias with a local spelling), and no resolved model id or packet version is shown. Line 137 presents cross-tier, same-family judging (sonnet over haiku in the contract fixtures) as independence.
apps/console/src/pages/simulator/quote.ts:23 A judge's quote is checked mechanically against the transcript line it cites, ±2 lines. Deterministic assertions sit outside the judgment.

apps/console/src/pages/simulator/Verdicts.tsx:87 The judge's account (its quotes) is checked against the artifact (the transcript), and the operator gets a second check independent of the daemon's (quote.ts:3-4).

apps/console/src/pages/simulator/Heatmap.tsx:182 Per-rule fail counts show their own denominator of runs that could have tripped them. Not-provoked and not-evaluable counts are shown in their own columns (Heatmap.tsx:73-74), so a detector that cannot fire does not read as a clean zero.

apps/console/src/pages/simulator/Heatmap.tsx:172 Void-judge and failed runs are counted apart from rule fails (instrument and harness failure kept out of the candidate's score). Failing rules list transcript refs for manual drill-down.
apps/console/src/pages/simulator/Tournaments.tsx:133 Instrument identity (hash) is shown and results from different hashes are never merged. compareCellKey also orders by instrument_hash first.
apps/console/src/pages/simulator/Heatmap.tsx:143 Matrix mode shows every cell, worst first, beside a tone×tier by segment×audience map. No headline winner hides the losing cells.
apps/console/src/pages/simulator/Tournaments.tsx:35 Despite the name, a tournament is a full factorial matrix, not a pairwise arena, so there is no pairing schedule to check.

pairs.registryProposal: judge-stability could say outright that a judge one capability tier above or below the candidate, within the same vendor family, is still an own-family judge. Projects use a 'never the same tier' rule as their independence guard, and the technique's own-family section does not name that substitute.
